### J-1 Node cap undercounts common Mermaid syntax, so oversized diagrams pass
- quote: "An ID is a token `[A-Za-z_][\w]*` that is an endpoint of an arrow"
- situation (adversary): `nodes` splits each line on ARROW and keeps only parts that are a bare ID. Mermaid has several common forms whose parts are not bare IDs, so those nodes are never counted.
- situation (correctness): `Alice->>John: Hello` leaves `John: Hello` after the split, which is not an ID, so John is not counted. `A --> B & C` and `A -- text --> B` are also missed. A sequence or state diagram with more than 20 participants can pass the cap. The test covers only flowchart chains.
- situation (consistency): a sequence diagram of 25 lines `Client->>Svc1: call` through `Client->>Svc25: call`. ARROW.split gives `Client` and `Svc1: call`; `Svc1: call` fails ID.fullmatch, so nodes() returns {Client}, one node, and the 20-node check passes a 26-node diagram. The same happens to `B` in `A -- retry --> B`, because `A -- retry` is not an ID.
- fix: parse the endpoints more strictly. Strip edge text and trailing `: ...`, split on `&` and `;`, and keep `DROP` within one line. Add tests for sequence, state, `&` and labelled-edge forms.
- validation: confirmed: implementation-E-1-adversary: the parsing of edge text, `&`, `;` and `: ...` is now right, and the sequence, state, `&` and labelled-edge tests were added. But `DROP` still runs over the whole block, so one unbalanced `"`, `(`, `[` or `{` in a line swallows every line up to the next closer. A valid sequence message such as `Client->>Svc3: retry (see note` followed by `Client->>Svc4: ok)` loses both lines before the `:` split ever runs. Those nodes are not counted, so an oversized diagram passes the AC-5 cap, which is the original symptom. No test covers it. Fix: apply `DROP` per line, `DROP.sub("", line)` inside the loop.; implementation-E-1-consistency: the listed steps (strip `: ...`, split `&` and `;`, DROP first) and their tests are in, but `A <--> B` still drops `A` and `A --o B` drops both endpoints, so the node cap still undercounts common flowchart syntax.; implementation-E-1-correctness: the parsing is stricter and the new forms are tested, but `DROP` is still applied to the whole block and can span lines, so one unbalanced quote or bracket still hides later nodes from the cap.
- disposition: fix-task by human: Fix it: clean labels one line at a time (DROP per line) and handle the remaining arrow forms (<-->, --o, --x, longer arrows), with a test for each, including an unbalanced quote/bracket.

### J-2 Any non-parse render failure becomes "unreachable", which skips the check and hides every later block
- quote: "after which no further block is rendered"
- situation (adversary): `render` returns "broken" only when the output contains the text `Parse error`. Other genuine diagram failures fall to "unreachable", for example an unknown diagram type from a typo like `flowchar TD`, a text-only block, or a mermaid runtime error. CT-4 turns "unreachable" into the note `render skipped: the renderer could not be fetched`, exit 0, and stops rendering every later block. One bad block early in the file therefore hides all later broken diagrams, with a misleading reason. Failures to start Chromium or to download it within the 120 s timeout take the same path. AC-9 ("fails naming that block as a broken diagram") is met only for parse errors.
- fix: separate "could not run" (npx missing, fetch failure, timeout, spawn error) from "ran and rejected the diagram". Treat the second as `broken` with the first error line. Keep skipping for the first only.
- validation: confirmed: render() returns "unreachable" for any non-zero exit without "Parse error", as CT-3 says ("any other failure"). A typo such as `flowchar TD` fails with an error other than Parse error. CT-4 then turns that into the "could not be fetched" note and stops rendering later blocks, so FR-11 and AC-9 are not met for it.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-18

### J-3 `check explainer` passes any existing file
- quote: "then it fails naming that block as a broken diagram"
- situation (adversary): `check` returns `[], []` for any `.md` file or slug that exists, including an empty file, a 21-node diagram or a broken diagram. `nio check explainer <slug>` exits 0 and prints no notes, so this is a silent pass. It is only safe if T-3 to T-5 land before anything relies on the command. The `explain.format` handling and the topic-mode distinction in CT-4 are also absent. Nothing marks the check as a stub. Unlike `explain finish`, it does not say "not built yet".
- fix: make the partial state loud (a note such as `checks not built yet`), or keep `explainer` out of the CLI choices until T-3 lands.

### J-4 `sections` drops `> ` lines from the walk-through and handles fences loosely
- quote: "lines starting `> ` and the record lines of the Data model"
- situation (adversary): any prose line starting `> ` is excluded from `walk`, not only the tool's own `> Broken diagram:` notes. A long walk-through written as a block quote passes the 120-word limit, and so does an empty one (which skips the "walk-through missing" rule). The Data model record-line exclusion is not implemented. Fences:
- fix: match the closing fence to the opener, and drop `> ` only when it is the tool's own note. Implement or remove the Data model rule.

### J-5 `render` runs `npx` from the caller's working directory
- quote: "running `npx -y MERMAID -i <temp .mmd> -o <out>`"
- situation (adversary): `subprocess.run` has no `cwd`. `npx` prefers a matching package in the cwd's `node_modules/.bin`, so the target project's own copy of mermaid-cli would run instead of the pinned 11.4.2. If it is not pinned, the first run downloads and executes a package in a repo the tool does not control. A cold fetch of Chromium may exceed 120 s. The timeout then reports "unreachable" (see F2), and the `npx` child may leave Chromium running.
- fix: run with `cwd` set to the temp directory. Give the timeout case its own note.

### J-9 A node whose ID starts with `end` is skipped
- quote: "lines starting `%%`, `classDef`, `class `, `style `, `linkStyle`, `click `, `subgraph` or `end` are skipped"
- quote: "SKIP = ("%%", "classDef", "class ", "style ", "linkStyle", "click ", "subgraph", "end")"
- situation (consistency): the flowchart line `endpoint --> api` starts with `end`, so `line.startswith(SKIP)` is true and both `endpoint` and `api` are dropped. A 25-node flowchart whose nodes are named `endpoint1 --> endpoint2` and so on counts zero nodes and passes the cap.
- fix: match the keyword `end` only as the whole word (the line equal to `end`, or `end` followed by a space), say so in CT-2, and add `endpoint --> api` to the self-check.
- validation: confirmed: implementation-E-1-consistency: the code now matches the whole word `end` and the self-check line is added, but CT-2 in `contracts.md` line 24 still lists `end` as a skipped line prefix and does not state the whole-word rule the fix asked for.
- disposition: accepted-risk by human: Accept as risk: code and test are right; CT-2's wording lags; note it for the next plan change.

### J-10 Broken-diagram reason is read from both streams, not stderr
- quote: "first stderr line holding Parse error"
- quote: "both = r.stdout + r.stderr"
- situation (consistency): when mermaid-cli writes its `Parse error` line to stdout, `render` returns that line as the reason, but CT-3 says the reason is the first stderr line. The same failing run gets a different reason from the one the spec names.
- fix: take the line from `r.stderr` only, as CT-3 says, or change CT-3 to say stdout or stderr and make the code and spec match.

### J-11 `sections()` returns a `diagram` key that CT-1 does not list
- quote: "{"title": str, "fence": str | None, "block": str | None, "walk": str, "drill": bool}"
- quote: "s["diagram"] = s.pop("img") or s["block"] is not None"
- situation (consistency): a consumer written from CT-1's Shape never learns that `diagram` exists, so the CT-4 "diagram section" check would recompute it from `fence` and `block` and could disagree with `sections()` on a section that has only a `![` line.

### J-12 SKIP prefix "end" drops any line starting with an ID like endpoint
- quote: "`SKIP = ("%%", "classDef", "class ", "style ", "linkStyle", "click ", "subgraph", "end")`"
- situation (correctness): `endpoint --> db` starts with "end" and is skipped entirely, so both IDs go uncounted. The same holds for `ending`, `endUser` and similar names.
- fix: match `end` only as the whole line, and `subgraph` only when followed by whitespace

### J-13 sections leaves the Data model record lines in walk
- quote: "the record lines of the Data model"
- situation (correctness): the contract says `walk` excludes the Data model's record lines. The code strips only fenced blocks, `![` lines and `> ` lines. A long Data model section would count its records toward the 120-word walk limit that T-3 enforces, and could fail a good explainer.
- fix: exclude the record lines in `sections`, or state in the contract that the Data model is exempt from the walk check
